title: Incompleteness
description: Any system strong enough to describe arithmetic contains truths it can never prove - reality included.

puzzle.goal: To let arithmetic talk about itself, every proof is turned into a single number. Symbol j of formula k has code c_kj; each formula becomes the product of successive primes raised to its codes, and the proof becomes the product of successive primes raised to those formula numbers. Write the logarithm of the proof's number for a proof of m formulas, formula k having n_k symbols.
puzzle.name: Gödel numbering of a proof
puzzle.form: sum ( k , 1 , m , ln ( p _ k ) * prod ( j , 1 , n _ k , p _ j ^ c _ kj ) )
puzzle.ask: A two-line proof: formula 1 has codes (a, b), formula 2 has the single code c. Find ln G.
puzzle.method: Unique prime factorisation makes the encoding reversible; the logarithm turns the outer product into a sum.
